title: A five-minute estimate: from users to servers and storage
captions: Start with users. 2 million daily users, each making about 20 requests, gives 40 million requests a day. Write this assumption down.
A day has 86,400 seconds. Round it to 100,000. 40 million ÷ 100,000 ≈ 400 requests per second on average. The exact answer is about 460, which is close enough.
Users do not arrive evenly. This example assumes dinner time brings 5 times the average. That is a guess; use real traffic data if you have it. The peak is about 2,000 QPS.
A load test shows one server handles about 500 QPS. The peak needs 4 servers. Add spare servers so that losing one, or a deploy, does not take you down.
Now storage: 500,000 orders a day at about 2 KB each is about 1 GB a day, or 365 GB a year. That fits in one database. The design stays simple.
